[&larr; Back to Datasets](../index.qmd)

The "final form" of this dataset evolved over a few stages:

* First, Jeff announced in class that the dataset would comprise [UN Comtrade](https://comtradeplus.un.org/) data merged with vessel arrival and departure data from [IMF PortWatch](https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/data-and-methodology). Unfortunately, Georgetown does not subscribe to Comtrade, so I'm unable to bulk-export that data
* Next, we tried the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's FAOSTAT ["Detailed Trade Matrix"](https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/TM): this dataset *is* available in full, but is **aggregated** to the (sender, receiver, product, year) level
* For the **microdata** we really want – so that we can simulate the kind of **individual financial transaction data** that you might encounter as a data scientist in **Retail Sales**, it turns out that Colombia's *Departamento Administrativo Nacional de Estadística (DANE)* provides individual-transaction level data!

With that note on the trajectory of this dataset out of the way, here is your vignette and accompanying sample midterm questions:

## Data Access

The Colombian Customs data is now available for DSAN 6000 students at the following S3 URI:

``` {.default}
s3://dsan6000-final/colombia-customs/
```

However, for "pointing" a **Spark cluster** at this dataset, you will need to use the `s3a://` prefix instead:

``` {.default}
s3a://dsan6000-final/colombia-customs/
```

Unlike the [NYC Shelter data](../nyc-shelters/index.qmd), where we have a single snapshot for the entire history of intakes, for this dataset we have **monthly snapshots** released by the Colombian government. So, the files within the bucket mirror this release structure, like:

``` {.default}
colombia-customs/
├─ Expo_2025/
│  ├─ 01_Enero/
│  │  ├─ Enero.csv
│  │  ├─ Enero.dta
│  │  ├─ Enero.sav
│  ├─ 02_Febrero/
│  │  ├─ Febrero.csv
│  │  ├─ Febrero.dta
│  │  ├─ Febrero.sav
│  │  ...
│  ├─ 12_Diciembre/
│  │  ├─ Diciembre.csv
│  │  ├─ Diciembre.dta
│  │  ├─ Diciembre.sav
├─ Impo_2025/
│  ├─ 01_Enero/
│  │  ├─ Enero.csv
│  │  ├─ Enero.dta
│  │  ├─ Enero.sav
│  ├─ 02_Febrero/
│  │  ├─ Febrero.csv
│  │  ├─ Febrero.dta
│  │  ├─ Febrero.sav
│  │  ...
│  ├─ 12_Diciembre/
│  │  ├─ Diciembre.csv
│  │  ├─ Diciembre.dta
│  │  ├─ Diciembre.sav
```

This pattern continues down to `Expo_2024`, `Impo_2024`, `Expo_2023`, `Impo_2023`, and so on, until it reaches **2012**, the first year for which digitized imports and exports are both available.

::: {.callout-warning title="Data Caveats"}

While cleaning the data for the DASN 6000 S3 bucket, I encountered the following issues with the original data (I will add more here if students find additional issues!):

* Export data for **December 2024** is missing from the original data (so is also missing in the S3 bucket)

:::

## Codebook

Here, for ease of use, I have taken the data files for 2025 imports and exports and **translated** the (abbreviated) column headers into simpler-to-understand English versions. The spelled-out versions of each variable (in Spanish) can be found [here](https://microdatos.dane.gov.co/index.php/catalog/472/datafile/F3), along with the *meaning* for each value of the numeric codes (for example, the country codes used for the `PAIS` and `BANDERA` variable). The translated codebooks are as follows:

### Exports (`Expo_2025` to `Expo_2012`)

| Column Name | Translation | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `FECH` | `date` | `FECH` is short for *fecha*, meaning **"date"**. Here, the date has **four digits**, where the first two represent the year and the second two represent the month: `YYMM`. |
| `ADUA` | `customs_house` | `ADUA` is short for *aduana*, meaning "customs house". Here, the specific sub-department of the customs declaration is encoded as an **integer**. Department `3`, for example, processed over 10K exports in January 2025, whereas department `27` processed only 1. (Note that all of the department codes may not used within a given year, meaning that you shouldn't assume that you can loop from `1` to `n`) |
| `PAIS` | `destination_country` | `PAIS` is the ASCII version of *país*, meaning "country". It is a **numeric** variable, a three-digit code representing the country that the good(s) were imported from / exported to. For example, imports from / exports to the United States have code `840`. |
| `COD_PAI4` | `destination_country_code` | For each value of `PAIS`, this value is the corresponding `string`-valued **three-letter code** for the country. For example, imports from / exports to the United States have `COD_PAI4` value `USA`. |
| `COD_SAL1` | `departure_point_code1` | `COD_SAL` and `COD_SAL1` are both short for *código lugar de salida*, meaning "departure point". `COD_SAL1` is a *numeric* (integer) code for the point of departure. For example, the port of [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia) is represented by `6`. |
| `COD_SAL` | `departure_point_code` | `COD_SAL` and `COD_SAL1` are both short for *código lugar de salida*, meaning "departure point". `COD_SAL` is a `string`-valued **three-letter code** for the point of departure. For example, the port of [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia) is represented as `"CTG"`. |
| `DPTO2` | `dept_of_origin` | Short for *departamento de procedencia*, Spanish for "department of origin". The meanings for each value are listed [here](https://microdatos.dane.gov.co/index.php/catalog/472/datafile/F3). |
| `VIA` | `transport_mode` | A numeric code for the mode of transport. The meanings for each value are listed [here](https://microdatos.dane.gov.co/index.php/catalog/472/datafile/F3) |
| `BANDERA` | `flag` | The nationality of the *transport vehicle* that is carrying out the shipment. Note that this is not the same as the destination country! (For example, a shipment destined for Mexico could be carried by a Fijian vessel) |
| `REGIM` | `customs_regime` | Import regime of the customs declaration. Note that this is `REGIMEN` in the export data! |
| `MODAD` | | |
| `FINALID` | | |
| `CER_ORI1` | | |
| `SISESP` | | |
| `POSAR` | `tariff_line` | Short for *posición arancelaria*, Spanish for "tariff classification". |
| `DPTO1` | `dept_of_origin_tariff` | Short for *departamento de origen por posición*, Spanish for "department of origin by position", but "position" here refers to the tariff line given by `POSAR` |
| `UNID` | `unit_code` | `UNID` is short for *unidad*, Spanish for "unit". It provides a *numeric code* for the unit of the quantity in the `CANTI` variable; for example, kilograms are represented by code `33` (the `CODUNI2` variable provides a more helpful `string`-format code). |
| `CODUNI2` | `unit` | Provides a more human-readable, `string`-formatted version of `UNID`; for example, `"KG"` for kilograms, which corresponds to the `UNID` value `33`. |
| `CANTI` | `quantity` | `CANTI` is short for *cantidad*, Spanish for "amount". The *unit* for the quantity is given by the `UNID` variable (as a numeric code), but more helpfully by the `CODUNI2` variable (as a string, like `"KG"` for kilograms). |
| `PBK` | `weight_kg_gross` | Short for *total kilos brutos de la posición*, Spanish for "gross weight in kilograms". The *gross* weight is the weight of the shipment *including* the packaging. |
| `PNK` | `weight_kg_net` | Short for *total kilos netos de la posición*, Spanish for "net weight in kilograms". The *net* weight is the weight of the shipment once the weight of the packaging is subtracted. |
| `FOBDOL` | `fob_value_usd` | The "Free on Board" (FOB) value, in US Dollars. |
| `FOBPES` | `fob_value_pesos` | The "Free on Board" (FOB) value, in Colombian Pesos. |
| `AGRENA` | | |
| `FLETES` | | |
| `SEGURO` | | |
| `OTROSG` | `other_expenses` | Short for *valor otros gastos de la posición*, Spanish for "value of other position-related expenses", where "position" again generally refers to the `POSAR` variable. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[5, 10, 85]"}

### Imports (`Impo_2025` to `Impo_2012`)

The corresponding (Spanish-language) listing of the full variable names can be found [here](https://microdatos.dane.gov.co/index.php/catalog/473/data-dictionary/F10?file_name=Enero), and the following table is again my attempt at translating and describing them!

| Column Name | Translation | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `FECH` | `date` | `FECH` is short for *fecha*, meaning **"date"**. Here, the date has **four digits**, where the first two represent the year and the second two represent the month: `YYMM`. |
| `ADUA` | `customs_house` | `ADUA` is short for *aduana*, meaning "customs house". Here, the specific sub-department of the customs declaration is encoded as an **integer**. Department `3`, for example, processed over 10K exports in January 2025, whereas department `27` processed only 1. (Note that all of the department codes may not used within a given year, meaning that you shouldn't assume that you can loop from `1` to `n`) |
| `PAISGEN` | `origin_country` | Short for *país origen*, meaning "country of origin". It is a **numeric** variable, a three-digit code representing the country that the good(s) were **produced**. For example, goods produced in the United States have code `840`. |
| `PAISPRO` | `provenance_country` | Short for *país de procedencia*, meaning "country of provenance". This seems similar to `PAISGEN` at first, but here the value is the country that the goods were **shipped from** (whereaas they may have been *produced* in a different country, indicated by the `PAISGEN` value). |
| `PAISCOM` | `purchase_country` | Short for *país de compra*, or country of purchase. Once again, this may be different from the country of production (`origin_country`) and country of provenance (`provenance_country`). |
| `DEPTODES` | `destination_department` | The customs house (within Colombia) receiving the goods |
| `VIATRANS` | `transport_mode` | Same as `VIA` in the export data (but, notice the difference in naming convention here, e.g. if you want to merge Impo and Expo at some point!) |
| `BANDERA` | `flag` | Same as in export data. |
| `REGIMEN` | `customs_regime` | Import regime of the customs declaration. Note that this is `REGIM` in the import data! |
| `ACUERDO` | `trade_agreement_code` | Preferential trade agreement claimed (if any) |
| `PBK` | `weight_kg_gross` | Same as in export data. |
| `PNK` | `weight_kg_net` | Same as in export data. |
| `CANU` | `quantity` | Same as `CANTI` in the export data. |
| `CODA` | `unit_code` | Same as `UNID` in the export data. |
| `NABAN` | `tariff_line` | Same as `POSAR` in the export data. |
| `VAFODO` | `fob_value` | The "Free on Board" (FOB) value, in USD (same as `fob_value_usd` in the export data). |
| `FLETE` | `freight` | |
| `VACID` | | |
| `VACIP` | | |
| `IMP1` | `vat_tax` | Sales tax (VAT) |
| `OTDER` | `other_duties` | Value of other duties. |
| `CLASE` | `importer_class` | Classification code for importer |
| `CUIDAIMP` | `importer_city` | City of importer |
| `CUIDAEXP` | `exporter_city` | City of exporter |
| `ACTECON` | `econ_activity_code` | Economic activity coding |
| `CODADAD` | `customs_admin_code` | Customs administration code |
| `VADUA` | `customs_value` | |
| `VRAJUS` | `adjustment_value` | Adjustment value |
| `BASEIVA` | `vat_base` | |
| `OTROSP` | `rate_other_charges` | |
| `OTROSBASE` | `base_other_charges` | |
| `TOTALIVAYO` | `total_vat_other` | Sum of VAT and other charges |
| `SEGUROS` | `insurance` | |
| `OTROSG` | `other_expenses` | |
| `LUIN` | `entry_place` | |
| `CODLUIN` | `entry_place_code` | |
| `DEPIM` | `importer_department` | |
| `COPAEX` | `exporter_country_code` | |
| `TIPOIM` | `import_type` | |
| `PORARA` | `tariff_rate` | (Unit is percentage) |
| `NIT` | `importer_tax_id` | |
| `DIGV` | `tax_id_check_digit` | |
| `RZIMPO` | `importer_name` | |
| `DEREL` | `tariff_duty_amount` | |
